# k0rdent_subnets (Data Source)

Every subnet inside one network, including the ones a cluster materialized.

This is how a configuration learns the CIDR a cluster was given, which is the value a firewall rule or a peering has to be written against.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The platform picks a cluster's CIDRs, so read them to write rules against.
data "k0rdent_subnets" "pods" {
  # The one network a cluster made for itself. one() fails the plan if there
  # isn't exactly one.
  network = one([for n in data.k0rdent_networks.all.networks : n.id if n.cluster_id != null])
}

resource "k0rdent_security_group" "from_pods" {
  id = "from-pods"

  # One ingress rule per CIDR. `ingress.value` is the current CIDR.
  dynamic "ingress" {
    for_each = data.k0rdent_subnets.pods.cidrs
    content {
      action             = "permit"
      protocol           = "tcp"
      source_prefix      = ingress.value
      destination_prefix = "0.0.0.0/0"

      destination_port_range = "443"
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `network` (String) Id of the network to read. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.

### Optional

- `display_name_regex` (String) Return only the subnets whose `display_name` matches this regular expression, in the RE2 syntax Terraform's own `regex` function takes. The match isn't anchored, so `prod` finds `preprod-a`: write `^prod-` for a prefix. One with no `display_name` never matches. Filtered in the provider, after the whole list is read: the list operation takes no such filter. **Constraints:** Must be a regular expression in RE2 syntax.
- `project` (String) Project to read. Defaults to the provider's `project`. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `region` (String) Region to read. Defaults to the provider's `region`. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `state` (String) Return only the subnets whose `state` is this value. Filtered in the provider, after the whole list is read: the list operation takes no such filter. **Constraints:** Value must be one of: ["creating" "active" "deleting" "failed"].
- `tags` (Map of String) Return only the subnets carrying every one of these tags with exactly this value. Tags beyond these don't matter. Filtered in the provider, after the whole list is read: the list operation takes no such filter. **Constraints:** Every tag value must be set: a null value matches nothing.

### Read-Only

- `cidrs` (List of String) Just the allocated blocks, sorted by the subnet's `id`, at the same positions as `subnets`.
- `subnets` (Attributes List) The subnets, sorted by `id`, which is the subnet's name. That order is stable when the platform reorders them but not when one is added, so reach an element with `for_each` rather than `subnets[0]`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--subnets))

<a id="nestedatt--subnets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `subnets`

Read-Only:

- `address_pool` (String) The pool the CIDR came from. Null on a cluster-provisioned subnet, whose CIDR came from the cluster lifecycle rather than a pool the tenant named.
- `cidr` (String) The allocated block. Empty until the subnet is `active`.
- `cluster_id` (String) UID of the cluster that provisioned it, if any.
- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name, for display only.
- `gateway` (String) Resolved gateway address, where one was allocated.
- `id` (String) The subnet's name.
- `prefix_length` (Number) Allocation prefix length.
- `self_link` (String) Platform-defined reference to this object.
- `state` (String) Lifecycle state as last read from the platform.
- `tags` (Map of String) User-defined labels, as key-value pairs. Null when the object has none.
